values: Content-Type (also `with.content_type`, written once) and Cache-Control are literal text. Other values may be `${{ }}` templates; a value that renders a line break or another control character, or more than 4096 bytes, fails the step with a 500 before anything is written, and a value that renders empty is not sent. Content-Disposition is `attachment` or `inline`, optionally `; filename="name.ext"` (no quote or backslash in the name). Vary and Link add to what the framework set; the others replace. On a flow only signed-in callers reach (`auth: required`, `role:` or `permissions:`), Cache-Control may not say `public`, `s-maxage`, or `max-age` without unqualified `private`/`no-store`. Every respond step for a signed-in caller, including on a public flow, emits `Cache-Control: private, no-store` regardless of authored freshness headers (Expires included), so a shared cache cannot reuse personal data.
error_status: Any app response with status 400 or above gets `no-store` added to its Cache-Control, including a public (`auth: none`) flow whose respond step declares a literal cacheable Cache-Control (`public, max-age=300` on a 404 or 410 becomes `public, max-age=300, no-store`, which no cache stores). The directive is added, never replacing what is there, so a handler's `private, no-store` stays. Successful answers keep their declared policy; a CDN-cached soft-404 needs a 200.
content_type: With no declared content type a respond step types the answer itself: application/json for `json:`, for a `body:` map or list, for a body written as a number or boolean and for a body that is exactly one `${{ }}`, and a text body from its template (see the `respond:` text bodies gotcha). A respond with no body (a status alone, an empty `body: ""`) sends an empty body and no Content-Type unless one is declared. With one, a text body (`body:` or `json:` written as text) is sent as written: a body that is exactly one `${{ }}` sends a text value as is (no JSON quotes), a number or boolean as its text, and a list or object JSON-encoded under a JSON type (application/json, */*+json) but fails the step under any other type. A `body:`/`json:` written as a map or list is always JSON, so it takes only a JSON type (another type is refused, and a deployed file keeps answering application/json). text/event-stream is refused. Values are substituted as they are, never HTML-escaped: a declared text/html (or SVG/XML) type on a body that holds request or row values serves those values as markup, so return data as JSON.
example:
- id: csv
        query: "SELECT group_concat(email, char(10)) AS text FROM waitlist"
      - run: respond
        with:
          status: 200
          content_type: "text/csv; charset=utf-8"
          headers:
            Content-Disposition: 'attachment; filename="waitlist.csv"'
            Cache-Control: "private, no-store"
          body: ${{ steps.csv.outputs.first.text }}
